neighbours.label: Chinese characters set inside an English or French sentence after a space (a Chinese word, name or a number followed by a Chinese character, inside Latin-script text); peaks on the first Chinese character, though some very common characters stay quiet. Near background for the same sentence written in English or in romanized pinyin. Known weaker leaks, not claimed: long plain Chinese, Korean or Arabic prose can reach about 0.3-0.4.
neighbours.short: Chinese characters inside a Latin-script sentence
neighbours.notes: Step-in reader of L34/N6623+ (drop 0.00 at single-unit zero ablation; on in 1 of its top examples). Probes: CJK after a space following a digit or Latin word 0.3-0.7, same text glued without a space ~0.16; which single characters fire depends on whether the tokenizer splits them into bytes (店 城 村 中 人 silent, 面 市 倍 fire). Feeders include byte-piece cells (machine guess '<0xE5>'). Test sentences written blind by a label-only author.
